activity_context.topic_title: Calculating the Position Function of a Particle Using Integration

feedback.worked_solution:
We start by integrating the velocity to get $x(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}x(t) & =\int v(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =\int {sec}^{2}⁡(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =\operatorname{tan}⁡(t)+C\end{aligned}
$$

To determine $C$, we use the fact that $x(\frac{\pi }{4})=2.$ Substituting this into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}2 & =\operatorname{tan}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4})+C \\ 2 & =1+C \\ C & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the position $x$ of the particle at time $t$ is 

$$
x(t)=\operatorname{tan}⁡(t)+1.
$$
